newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Singer Bangladesh seen offering bonus, dividend.
newsitem.headline: Singer Bangladesh seen offering bonus, dividend.

text.p: Singer Bangladesh Limited is expected to pay a 75 percent dividend and may offer a one-for-one bonus share issue for 1996, company officials said on Monday.
The company paid an 81 percent cash dividend and made a one-for-one bonus share issue last year.
The annual meeting is set for Wednesday. Singer Bangladesh is a subsidiary of Singer International Limited.
Mahbub Jamil, chairman of Singer Bangladesh, said political chaos and uncertainties during the first half of the year had affected the company's operations. "As a result growth slowed," he added.
Net profit rose 32.38 percent to 139.24 million taka in 1996 compared with a 55.5 percent jump to 105.02 million the previous year.
"But we have been able to meet our annual target due to planning and hard work," Jamil told Reuters.
Turnover increased 13.26 percent to 1.143 billion taka in 1996. Shareholders' equity shot up to 217.22 million taka compared with 161.08 million taka the previous year.
"There was a sharp increase in the value of the stock in the capital market which hit 16,670 taka" against 5,950 taka at the end of 1995, said Khurshid Alam, a director of the company.
The company's product line includes sewing machines, television sets, videocassette players, washing machines, refrigerators, air-conditioners and other electrical appliances.
"We further intend to focus on product performance, price and market demands," Jamil said.
Alam added: "Our mission is to improve the quality of life of people by providing comforts at affordable prices. We will continue to honour and maintain high ethical standards."
The share was traded at 6,333.55 taka on Sunday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
